intervals.label: operating
intervals.quote: The PS first accelerated protons on 24 November 1959, becoming for a brief period the world's highest energy particle accelerator.

beam_energy.quote: The accelerator operates at up to 26 GeV.

circumference.quote: With a circumference of 628 metres, the PS has 277 conventional (room-temperature) electromagnets, including 100 dipoles to bend the beams round the ring.

summary.plain: CERN's oldest working accelerator, a 628-metre ring that first accelerated protons in 1959. For a short time it was the most powerful accelerator in the world, and it still feeds every beam that ends up in the Large Hadron Collider.
summary.technical: 628 m proton synchrotron, 277 room-temperature magnets (100 dipoles), top energy 26 GeV; accepts 2 GeV protons from the PS Booster or ions from LEIR and injects into the SPS.
